title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The typed text is not part of the 1975–76 divided-power de Rham notes. It is a reused typescript sheet, page 170 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), from the section on the complex-analytic case (numbering 13.2.1.1). Grothendieck wrote his later notes on the blank side of such sheets. The blue handwritten lines at the bottom belong to the current notes.

Setting of the typed text: S is a complex analytic space and s a point of S. E and E' are vector bundles on S. R ⊂ E and R' ⊂ E' are sub-local-systems of lattices, so that E/R and E'/R' are families of complex tori. Hypothesis b) concerns R being locally constant / of the right rank. Hypothesis c) says that the fibre R_s = R_o generates the fibre of E at s.

Claim (map 13.2.1.1): germs at s of homomorphisms E → E' sending R into R' correspond bijectively to coherent systems of homomorphisms E_n → E'_n sending R_n into R'_n. Here E_n, R_n are the restrictions to the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of s. In other words, homomorphisms of germs of tori agree with homomorphisms of their formal completions.

Proof as typed:
- Coherent systems E_n → E'_n are the same as Ô_s-linear maps F̂ : Ê_s → Ê'_s. Germs of maps are the same as O_s-linear maps F : E_s → E'_s.
- Since O_s → Ô_s is faithfully flat and the modules are free, the map is injective.
- Surjectivity: suppose F̂ respects all R_n. By c) and Nakayama, R_o generates Ê_s. Here R_o is read either as formal sections of R̂ over Ŝ or as germs of sections of R; these agree because R is locally constant.
- So it suffices to show F̂(R_o) ⊂ E'_s. But F̂(R_o) ⊂ R'_o, and R'_o consists of germs of genuine (convergent) sections of R' ⊂ E'.
- Hence F̂ descends to a germ F with F(R_o) ⊂ R'_o. The page breaks off as hypothesis b) is about to be used to show that F maps R into R' on a neighbourhood.

This is a formal-to-analytic algebraization result for homomorphisms of families of complex tori. It serves the complex-analytic comparison in SGA 7 IX (Néron models, monodromy, analytic description of degenerating abelian varieties).

Handwritten blue lines (from the current notes): a diagram DR(A^{1,0}_*, T) → A^{**}, with arrows to and from DR(P_* ⊗_Z A_0, T). This matches the neighbouring pages. There Grothendieck is building a map v from a divided-power de Rham algebra DR(A^{1,0}_*, T) into a bigraded divided-power algebra Â'^{**}, with v(1,0)(T) = T, presumably to show that certain groupoids of divided-power de Rham structures are connected.
errors: No mathematical error. The Nakayama step is correct: generation of the fibre E(s) by R_s implies generation of the free modules E_s and Ê_s. The identification of formal sections of R̂ with germs of sections of R needs R to be locally constant, which hypothesis b) or the setting presumably supplies. The proof is incomplete on this page because it continues on the next typescript page, which is not present.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms of germs of families of complex tori (E/R) agree with compatible homomorphisms on all infinitesimal neighbourhoods; proved via Nakayama, using that the lattice generates the fibre and consists of convergent sections.
ideas.modern_name: Formal–analytic comparison (algebraization) of homomorphisms of families of complex tori / degenerating abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (1967–69; publ. 1972)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §13 (complex-analytic case), around 13.2.1

ideas.what: Handwritten scrap: comparison map between the divided-power de Rham algebra DR(A^{1,0}, T) and a bigraded algebra A^{**}, and a variant DR(P ⊗_Z A_0, T).
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the divided-power de Rham complex / crystalline-type comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot, Illusie (crystalline and de Rham–Witt context, 1970s)

deep.surprise_reason: The typed text is a reused page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX and contains a standard Nakayama/algebraization argument. The handwritten fragment is too sketchy to carry new content beyond the neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: '(où E_s et E'_s sont ...)': both E_s and E'_s should be underlined (sheaf-theoretic fibres), i.e. \underline{E}_s and \underline{E}'_s.
The typed page is SGA 7 Exp. IX p.170 reused as scrap; '488' is the archive stamp and '104' the folio. The faint mirrored '488' visible through the paper is bleed-through, not text.

Handwritten line is probably 'DR(A^{1,0}_*, T) → A^{**}' with 'DR' struck and rewritten. The lower line is 'DR(P_* ⊗_Z A_0, T)' (P possibly overwritten), consistent with the next page's \widehat{DR}(A^{10}_*, T).
